instruction: Change Chrome's startup behavior to continue where you left off.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Chrome menu, navigated to Settings > Privacy and security, explored third-party cookies, site settings, on-startup page, searched 'clear on exit' in settings, then tried chrome://flags with various queries. Never found the auto-delete browsing data setting.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome three-dot menu, navigate to chrome://settings, click sidebar sections (Privacy and security, On start-up), use settings search bar, navigate to chrome://flags and search flags
metadata.failure_analysis: Model could not locate the 'Delete browsing data on close' setting. Searched in wrong areas (cookies, site settings, flags) instead of finding the correct path.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to changing startup behavior on the On start-up page, which the model already navigated to successfully (screenshot 25). Tests model's ability to select a radio button in settings.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing Chrome startup to 'Continue where you left off'. Evaluator reads Chrome Preferences file and checks session.restore_on_startup == 5.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter get_new_startup_page correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and checks session.restore_on_startup == 5, which corresponds to 'Continue where you left off' startup behavior.
Metric exact_match correctly compares getter result string 'true' against expected string 'true' from rules.
Data flow is correct: get_rule returns {'expected': 'true'}, getter returns 'true'/'false' string, exact_match compares them.
Coverage is complete: the single instruction requirement (change startup to continue where you left off) is fully verified.

Minor concern: getter returns 'true' when no 'session' key exists in Preferences (assuming fresh-start mode), which could be a false positive if Chrome hasn't been configured. However, since Chrome is launched in config, the session key should exist in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider that the getter's fallback of returning 'true' when no 'session' key exists could cause false positives in edge cases where Chrome Preferences lacks the session key. A stricter check would return 'false' when the session key is absent, since 'Continue where you left off' requires an explicit restore_on_startup=5 setting.
